newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-TAYLOR OPTIMISTIC DESPITE PERSONAL CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR OPTIMISTIC DESPITE PERSONAL CRISIS.

text.p: Australia's beleaguered captain Mark Taylor remained outwardly confident on the eve of the first Ashes test starting at Edgbaston on Thursday.
Taylor, short of runs and under fire from several former Australian test skippers, said on Wednesday: "You've got to ride the bumps, and sometimes pull the knives out of your back.
"It hasn't been a pleasant time for me, so I'm looking forward to the game starting, so we can focus on that. I'm only one innings away from shutting everybody up."
There was certainly no lack of confidence as Taylor reeled off the names of the 11 to face England, 24 hours before he needed to.

Greg Blewett, who made a century in his only first-class innings of the tour to date, was confirmed ahead of Justin Langer, and seam bowler Michael Kasprowicz was given his third test cap in preference to Brendon Julian.
"It's the best all-round side and the form side," said Taylor.
Taylor's view that "England seem to be more buoyant" was echoed by his opposite number Michael Atherton.
England's captain said: "There's a huge amount of expectancy and we're really looking forward to it."
Atherton, who equals Peter May's record of captaining England in 41 tests, has been stressing to his players the need to "grab the initiative early on".
In the last five Ashes series, the side winning the first match has taken the series.
Groundsman Steve Rouse, aware that test cricket could be taken away from Edgbaston if the quality of the pitch does not improve, said the recent good weather would help.
And both captains believe it will be a better surface than for the previous tests against West Indies and India which ended within three and four days respectively.
